channel.title: Le Monde de l'éducation - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Le Monde de l'éducation (lemonde.fr)

item.title: Mette Frederiksen heads into Danish elections as a global figure, but a divisive one domestically
item.description: In power since 2018, the leader of the Social Democrats is seeking re-election on Tuesday. While her support for Ukraine and her firm stance against Donald Trump regarding Greenland have earned her recognition on the European stage, her party has been struggling in the polls.

item.title: EU and Australia strike free trade deal after years of talks
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen and Anthony Albanese announced a compromise in Canberra aimed at boosting exports and strengthening economic ties amid global trade uncertainty.

item.title: Five affordable vegetarian restaurants in the Paris region
item.description: Craving a quinoa arancini, an Asian-inspired salad or a coconut dessert? Here is our selection of places in Paris and the suburbs where you can enjoy quality vegetarian food for under €20.

item.title: Emmanuel Grégoire's long run to Paris City Hall
item.description: The next mayor of Paris, who will be officially elected by the city council on Sunday, will now step into the spotlight after years in the shadow of his political mentors.

item.title: France's Socialists in turmoil over alliances with LFI as presidential race looms
item.description: Socialist leader Olivier Faure has faced criticism from internal rivals, including former president François Hollande, over the party's 'zigzagging' on alliances with the radical-left La France Insoumise.

item.title: Trump steps back from his own Iran ultimatum
item.description: The US president postponed his deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming talks are underway with the regime, which Iranian officials deny.

item.title: French judge probes former EU border chief for complicity in crimes against humanity
item.description: Fabrice Leggeri, now a far-right member of the European Parliament, was accused of tolerating pushbacks of asylum seekers during a seven-year spell as Frontex chief that began in 2015.

item.title: In southern Lebanon, civilians are trapped after Israel destroys bridges
item.description: The Israeli military is seeking to isolate southern Lebanon, a Hezbollah stronghold, from the rest of the country. Now, only one access route connects Tyre's remaining 20,000 residents and displaced people to the capital.

item.title: Iran names ex-IRGC commander to succeed Larijani as security chief
item.description: After Supreme National Security Council head Ali Larijani was killed in an Israeli strike, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, a long-serving former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander, has been appointed to succeed him.

item.title: Italy: Giorgia Meloni's failed gamble on judicial reform
item.description: By overwhelmingly voting against the referendum pushed by Italian PM Giorgia Meloni, a majority of Italians have expressed their attachment to a certain vision of democracy and to the constitution forged after Mussolini's dictatorship.
